title: Bounded Type Parameters: Enforcing Upper Bounds
summary: Restrict type arguments using <T extends Number>: invoking methods of the bound without casting, and preventing unsupported types.
learningObjectives: Apply upper bounded type parameter syntax: <T extends UpperBound>
Invoke methods defined on the bound directly on generic variables without casting
Enforce multiple bounds using intersection syntax: <T extends Number & Comparable<T>>
Understand the class-first rule in multiple bounds syntax and why multiple classes are prohibited
expectedOutcomes: Ability to design domain-restricted generic algorithms (numeric analyzers, comparable sorters)
Mastery of intersection types and compile-time API constraints

activities.title: Practical Context: Electric Vehicle High-Voltage Charging Connector

analogy.headline: Practical Context: Electric Vehicle High-Voltage Charging Connector
analogy.story:
A Level-3 DC Fast Charger cannot accept just any machine with wheels: a bicycle, diesel truck, or lawnmower cannot plug in. The charging station protocol is bounded: ChargingStation<T extends ElectricVehicle & FastChargeCapable>.

Because of this bound, the charger knows with absolute certainty before sending electricity that any vehicle plugged into the port possesses a battery management system (`battery.requestVoltage()`) and thermal cooling circuits (`cooling.verifyTemperature()`). The charging protocol interacts with those verified subsystems directly without guesswork or adapters.
analogy.keyTakeaway: An upper bound restricts generic types to a specific inheritance hierarchy, guaranteeing that methods of the bound are available at compile-time.

activities.title: Upper Bound Mechanics: Single Bounds, Methods Access & Intersection Types

keyTakeaways: Upper bound syntax <T extends Bound> restricts type arguments to Bound or its subclasses/implementations
The keyword 'extends' is used for BOTH classes and interfaces in generic bounds (never 'implements')
Methods defined on the bound can be invoked directly on T variables without explicit casting
Multiple bounds use the ampersand (&) operator: <T extends SuperClass & InterfaceA & InterfaceB>
In multiple bounds, a class (if present) MUST be declared first; multiple classes are forbidden

activities.title: Comparable Min/Max Bounded Search
activities.description: Trace a generic boundary search algorithm constrained by Comparable<T>.

steps.description: Declare <T extends Comparable<T>>. This guarantees every instance of T can compare itself against another T.
Invoke current.compareTo(min). The compiler validates this call statically without reflection or casts.
Works seamlessly for String, Integer, LocalDate, or any custom class implementing Comparable.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to declare that type parameter T must implement the interface Serializable?
questions.explanation: In Java generic type parameters, the 'extends' keyword is used universally for both classes and interfaces. The 'implements' keyword is not legal in generic parameter declarations.

questions.question: What is wrong with the declaration '<T extends Cloneable & Number>'?
options: A generic type cannot implement Cloneable
In multiple bounds syntax, a class (Number) must be specified first before any interfaces (Cloneable)
The ampersand (&) operator is only allowed in boolean expressions
Number is final and cannot be extended
questions.explanation: In multiple bounds (<T extends A & B>), if one of the bounds is a class, it must appear first: <T extends Number & Cloneable>. Specifying an interface before a class causes a compile-time syntax error.

activities.title: Senior Engineer Interview: Recursive Type Bounds

qaList.question: What is a Recursive Type Bound, why is '<T extends Comparable<T>>' declared this way, and what problem does it solve?
qaList.answer: A recursive type bound is a type parameter that is bounded by an expression containing the type parameter itself, most commonly '<T extends Comparable<T>>'. This idiom states: 'T can be compared to other instances of T (mutually comparable)'. Without the recursive bound, if it were simply '<T extends Comparable>', T would implement raw Comparable and compareTo would accept Object, sacrificing compile-time type safety. With '<T extends Comparable<T>>', the compiler guarantees that 'a.compareTo(b)' can only compare objects of the exact same type T, rejecting mismatched comparisons (like comparing a String to an Integer) at compile time.

activities.title: Self-Evaluation Checklist
checklist: I know how to restrict type parameters using <T extends UpperBound>
I know why 'extends' is used for both classes and interfaces in generic declarations
I understand the class-first rule in multiple bounds (<T extends Class & Interface>)
I understand recursive type bounds like <T extends Comparable<T>>

practiceProblems.title: Generic Range Checker for Numbers
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a class NumberRange<T extends Number & Comparable<T>> with methods contains(T value) that checks if value is between min and max (inclusive) using compareTo().

practiceProblems.title: Sum of Squares for Numeric Types
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method sumOfSquares(List<T> numbers) for <T extends Number> that calculates the sum of the squares of each number as a double.

practiceProblems.title: Generic Binary Search on Comparable Array
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method binarySearch(T[] sortedArray, T key) for <T extends Comparable<T>> that returns the index of key, or -1 if not found.

practiceProblems.title: Generic Value Clamping Utility
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method clamp(T value, T low, T high) for <T extends Comparable<T>> that restricts value to the range [low, high].

practiceProblems.title: Second Largest in Unique Comparable Array
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Implement a generic static method findSecondLargest(T[] array) for <T extends Comparable<T>> that returns the second largest distinct element, or null if array has fewer than 2 distinct elements.
